tierWindow.goal: Use AI critically on real study tasks: decide when and how to bring a tool in, prompt it well, and check what it gives you before you rely on it.
tierWindow.cognitiveDemand: Application and analysis: apply AI to a task, refine your approach, and appraise the output (use, apply, refine, check, judge).
tierWindow.taskComplexity: Realistic study tasks with more than one right approach; judgement calls about fit, prompting and verification rather than single settled facts.
tierWindow.autonomy: Moderate scaffolding: worked examples and checklists, but the learner makes the decisions and applies the moves to their own work.

decidedValue.priorExperienceAnchor: The learner already has the AI literacy foundations the introductory tier builds: they know what generative AI tools are, roughly how they work, and have tried a chatbot. They have not yet built a disciplined, critical way of bringing AI into real study tasks. Teach the judgement and habits for using AI well, not the basics of what it is.

Understanding what AI is belongs to the introductory tier; evaluating, creating with and acting ethically around AI at depth belongs to the advanced tier.

decidedValue.signpostBody: The course has three short lessons. First, fitting AI to the task: deciding whether and how to use a tool. Second, prompting and refining: getting useful output. Third, checking what AI gives you: verifying it before you rely on it. Work through them in order; each builds on the one before.
decidedValue.signpostInstruction: Work through the three lessons in order.
decidedValue.overview:
This short course is about using AI well in your studies. You already know what generative AI tools are and have probably tried one. The question now is how to use them critically on real study tasks, so they help your learning rather than get in its way.

By the end you will be able to decide when and how to bring an AI tool into a task, write and refine prompts that get useful output, and check what the tool gives you before you rely on it. These are practical habits you can use this week, in any subject.
decidedValue.courseOutcomesFraming: Three course outcomes framed up front: decide when and how to use AI, prompt and refine for useful output, and check AI output before relying on it.

practiceConnection.academic: Using AI well is becoming part of academic work in every subject. Tutors increasingly expect you to know when a tool helps and when it does not, to get useful output from it, and to check that output rather than trust it. Build these habits now and they carry into every module, and into professional work where AI is already a daily tool.

grounding.note: W-OPEN states the three course outcomes and why they matter (AL-5)

decidedValue.whereNextBody: Two directions build on this. Going deeper: the advanced AI and technology course takes you into evaluating tools and systems, creating substantial work with AI, and the wider ethics of its use. Going wider: these habits support every other pathway, from Academic Writing and Criticality to Researching, wherever you bring a tool into real academic work.
decidedValue.summary: You have reached the end of the course. Using AI is no longer a matter of habit: it is something you can do on purpose. You can decide when and how a tool fits a task, and when to keep it out. You can prompt a tool with context, task and format, and refine when the first answer falls short. And you can check what it gives you for accuracy, bias and integrity before you rely on it. Look back at the confidence check: comparing where you started with where you are now shows how far this has moved.

practiceConnection.academic: From here, using AI critically is something you practise in every module. Each time you choose whether a tool fits, each prompt you refine, each answer you check before trusting it, is this skill at work. It is also what study and professional life increasingly reward: people who can use these tools well, and know when not to, rather than leaning on them blindly.
